image_description: A close-up, front-facing view of a single circular loudspeaker driver (woofer) with a grey metallic or plastic frame. The cone is dark grey/black with a central dust cap. There are mounting holes around the perimeter of the frame. The background is plain white.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows only the speaker driver unit itself, not the full enclosure/box. The enclosure is effectively out of frame or non-existent in this crop.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: One or more circular speaker cones on front face of varying sizes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A single circular speaker cone is clearly visible and dominates the image.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Prominent large woofer dominating the front face with a much smaller tweeter positioned above or beside it.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While a woofer is present, there is no tweeter visible in the image. The checkpoint specifies a system with both; this is just a component.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Cone surface made of paper, polypropylene, or composite with rubber surround.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The texture appears consistent with standard speaker cone materials, and a flexible surround is visible connecting the cone to the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Grille cloth or perforated metal may cover the drivers.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The driver is exposed; no grille is present. This is acceptable per 'may cover', but strictly speaking, the feature is absent.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Terminal connections visible on rear panel.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a front view; the rear panel is completely occluded.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wood, MDF, or plastic enclosure with black, white, or wood-grain finish.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: No enclosure is visible, only the driver frame which appears to be metal or hard plastic.
The object is clearly identifiable as a speaker driver.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The cone surface has an overly smooth, airbrushed gradient appearance lacking the fine micro-texture typical of paper or polypropylene cones. It looks slightly synthetic.
The mounting holes around the rim are irregular in shape and spacing. Some appear partially melted or distorted rather than being clean punched circles, suggesting geometric instability.
The elliptical perspective of the outer rim seems slightly inconsistent with the inner cone geometry, creating a subtle warping effect.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific type of audio component and rule out misclassification as a generic wheel or mechanical part.
To verify the structural integrity of the mounting holes and the boundary between the cone and the surround, checking for melting or fusion artifacts.
To assess the realism of the material textures (metal vs plastic vs paper) and identify any subtle rendering artifacts.

focus_areas: Regularity and sharpness of mounting holes
Texture realism of the speaker cone
Boundary definition between cone, surround, and frame
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the mounting holes on the speaker frame. AI generators often struggle with repetitive geometric features like screw holes, leading to distortion or irregular shapes. Also, evaluate if the cone texture looks physically plausible or too digitally smooth.
